daas-irab:1-1.t: ﴿سَبِّحِ﴾: an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿اسْمَ رَبِّكَ﴾: اسم is mafʿūl bihi (direct object), muḍāf to ربك; ﴿الْأَعْلَى﴾: naʿt (adjective) of ربك; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya) and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:2-2.t: ﴿الَّذِي﴾: a second naʿt (adjective) of ربك; ﴿خَلَقَ﴾: a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); ﴿فَسَوَّى﴾: conjoined to خلق.

daas-irab:3-3.t: The clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:4-4.t: The clause is also conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:5-5.t: ﴿فَجَعَلَهُ﴾: a past verb and its first object, the fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir); ﴿غُثاءً﴾: second mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿أَحْوى﴾: ḥāl (circumstantial) from المرعى; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:6-6.t: ﴿سَنُقْرِئُكَ﴾: the sīn is for the future, and an imperfect verb and its object, the fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir); the clause is resumptive. ﴿فَلا تَنْسى﴾: the fāʾ is a particle of reason, لا is negative, and an imperfect verb whose agent is latent.

daas-irab:7-7.t: ﴿إِلَّا﴾: a particle of exception; ﴿ما﴾: a relative noun in the position of an accusative as the excepted; ﴿شاءَ اللَّهُ﴾: a past verb, and the Name of Majesty is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿إِنَّهُ﴾: inna and its noun; ﴿يَعْلَمُ﴾: an imperfect verb whose agent is latent (mustatir); ﴿الْجَهْرَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of inna, and the nominal clause gives the reason (taʿlīl) and has no grammatical position. ﴿وَما﴾: a relative noun conjoined to الجهر; ﴿يَخْفى﴾: an imperfect verb whose agent is latent; the clause is the ṣila.

daas-irab:8-8.t: ﴿وَنُيَسِّرُكَ﴾: an imperfect verb and its object, the fāʿil (agent) being latent (mustatir); ﴿لِلْيُسْرى﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:9-9.t: ﴿فَذَكِّرْ﴾: the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ indicating an implied condition), and an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is the apodosis of an implied condition and has no grammatical position. ﴿إِنْ﴾: a conditional particle that puts the verb in the jussive; ﴿نَفَعَتِ﴾: a past verb in the position of a jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); ﴿الذِّكْرى﴾: agent; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya) and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:10-10.t: ﴿سَيَذَّكَّرُ﴾: the sīn is for the future, and an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ); ﴿مَنْ﴾: a relative noun, its fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive. ﴿يَخْشى﴾: an imperfect verb whose agent is latent (mustatir); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause).

daas-irab:11-11.t:
[Translator's note: the Arabic source text of this entry is garbled (the brackets and opening letters of the quoted words are lost: «َ يَتَجَنَّبُهَا»», «لْأَشْقَى»»); the quoted words are restored from the verse وَيَتَجَنَّبُهَا الْأَشْقَى.]
﴿وَيَتَجَنَّبُهَا﴾: an imperfect verb and its object; ﴿الْأَشْقَى﴾: fāʿil (agent); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:12-12.t: ﴿الَّذِي﴾: a relative noun, naʿt (adjective) of الأشقى; ﴿يَصْلَى﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿النَّارَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿الْكُبْرى﴾: adjective of النار; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause).

daas-irab:13-13.t: ﴿ثُمَّ﴾: a conjunction; ﴿لا﴾: negative; ﴿يَمُوتُ﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿فِيها﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; ﴿وَلا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; ﴿وَلا﴾: negative; ﴿يَحْيى﴾: conjoined to يموت.

daas-irab:14-14.t: ﴿قَدْ﴾: a particle of verification (taḥqīq); ﴿أَفْلَحَ﴾: a past verb; ﴿مَنْ﴾: its fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive. ﴿تَزَكَّى﴾: a past verb whose agent is latent (mustatir); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause).

daas-irab:15-15.t: ﴿وَذَكَرَ﴾: a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); ﴿اسْمَ رَبِّهِ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), muḍāf to ربه; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; ﴿فَصَلَّى﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and صلى is conjoined to ذكر.

daas-irab:16-16.t: ﴿بَلْ﴾: a conjunction; ﴿تُؤْثِرُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), the wāw being its fāʿil (agent); ﴿الْحَياةَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); ﴿الدُّنْيا﴾: naʿt (adjective).

daas-irab:17-17.t: ﴿وَالْآخِرَةُ خَيْرٌ﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and أبقى is conjoined to the khabar.

daas-irab:18-18.t: ﴿إِنَّ هذا﴾: inna and its noun; ﴿لَفِي الصُّحُفِ﴾: the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and في الصحف is the khabar (predicate) of inna; ﴿الْأُولى﴾: naʿt (adjective); the clause is resumptive and has no grammatical position.

daas-irab:19-19.t: ﴿صُحُفِ﴾: badal (substitute) for الصحف; ﴿إِبْراهِيمَ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); ﴿وَمُوسى﴾: conjoined to إبراهيم.

farraa:1-1.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿سَبِّحِ ٱسْمَ رَبِّكَ﴾, and ﴿باسم ربك﴾.
Both of these have occurred, and it is of the speech of the Arabs.

farraa:3-3.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلَّذِي قَدَّرَ فَهَدَىٰ﴾.
He determined His creation, and guided the male of the beasts to the way of approaching the female.
It is also said: He determined and guided and led astray; so mention of guidance sufficed for mention of misguidance, because of how often it accompanies it. The readers are agreed on the doubled form (قدّر). Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī used to read قَدَر, lightened, and they consider it to be from the reading of ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib (may Allah have mercy on him) [135/a]. The doubled form is dearer to me because the readers agree on it.

farraa:5-7.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَجَعَلَهُ غُثَآءً أَحْوَىٰ﴾.
When vegetation becomes dry, it is غثاء (stubble). الأحوى: what has turned black from age. It may also be: He brought forth the pasture dark green (أحوى), then made it stubble; so it is placed later while its meaning is earlier.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿سَنُقْرِئُكَ فَلاَ تَنسَىٰ إِلاَّ مَا شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ﴾.
He did not will that he should forget anything. It is like His saying: ﴿خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا مَا دَامَتِ السَّماوَاتُ والأَرْضُ إِلاَّ مَا شَاءَ رَبُّك﴾, and He does not will [otherwise]. You would say in speech: "I will surely give you all that you ask, except what I will" and "unless I will to deny you", while the intention is not to deny him. On this pattern run the oaths in which an exception is made, while the swearer's intention is fulfilment.

farraa:11-11.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted is He: ﴿وَيَتَجَنَّبُهَا ٱلأَشْقَى﴾.
He avoids the reminder and does not take heed.

farraa:12-12.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿ٱلنَّارَ ٱلْكُبْرَىٰ﴾.
It is the lowest of the layers of the Fire.

farraa:14-14.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَن تَزَكَّىٰ﴾.
He did good and gave charity. It is also said: قد أفلح من تزكى: he gave charity before going out on the day of the Eid.

farraa:15-15.t:
﴿وَذَكَرَ ٱسْمَ رَبِّهِ فَصَلَّىٰ﴾.
He attended the prayer with the imam.

farraa:16-16.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿بَلْ تُؤْثِرُونَ ٱلْحَيَاةَ ٱلدُّنْيَا﴾.
The readers agreed on the tāʾ. In the reading of Ubayy it is: "بَلْ أَنْتُمْ تُؤْثِرُونَ الْحَياةَ", a confirmation for whoever [«لم» in the source, read «لمن»] read with tāʾ.
Some readers read: "بَلْ يُؤْثِرُونَ".

farraa:18-18.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّ هَـٰذَا لَفِي ٱلصُّحُفِ ٱلأُولَىٰ﴾.
He says: whoever mentions the name of his Lord and prays and does good — that is in the former scriptures just as it is in the Qur'an.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Aʿlā
Meccan
﷽
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿سَبِّحِ اسْمَ رَبِّكَ الأعْلى﴾ ("glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High"): that is, declare your Lord free of every evil, and say: ”سُبْحانَ رَبِّيَ الأعْلى“ ("Glory be to my Lord, the Most High").

zajjaj:2-2.t: ﴿الَّذِي خَلَقَ فَسَوّى﴾ ("Who created and proportioned"): He created the human being well-proportioned, made him bear witness against himself that He is his Lord, and created him upon the natural disposition (fiṭra).

zajjaj:3-3.t: And His saying: ﴿والَّذِي قَدَّرَ فَهَدى﴾ ("and Who determined and guided"): He guided him to the way, whether grateful or ungrateful. One of the grammarians said: [it means] "and guided and led astray", but ”وَأضَلَّ“ ("and led astray") was omitted because there is evidence for it in the discourse; He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ”يُضِلُّ مَن يَشاءُ ويَهْدِي مَن يَشاءُ“ ("He leads astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills").

zajjaj:4-5.t: ﴿والَّذِي أخْرَجَ المَرْعى﴾ ﴿فَجَعَلَهُ غُثاءً أحْوى﴾: ”أحْوى“ is in the position of the accusative (fī mawḍiʿ naṣb), a ḥāl (circumstantial) of ”اَلْمَرْعى“. The meaning is: ”اَلَّذِي أخْرَجَ المَرْعى أحْوى“ ("Who brought forth the pasture dark"), that is, He brought it forth green, tending toward ḥuwwa; and ”اَلْحُوَّةُ“ is blackness. ﴿فَجَعَلَهُ غُثاءً أحْوى﴾: He dried it until He turned it into dry, broken stubble, like the scum (ghuthāʾ) you see on top of floodwater.

zajjaj:6-6.t: His saying: ﴿سَنُقْرِئُكَ فَلا تَنْسى﴾ ﴿إلا ما شاءَ اللَّهُ﴾ [al-Aʿlā: 7] ("We shall make you recite, and you will not forget, except what Allah wills"): Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that He would give the Prophet ﷺ a sign by which his distinction would be made clear: that Gabriel, peace be upon him, descends to him with revelation while he is unlettered, neither writing a book nor reading it, and he teaches his Companions to recite and forgets nothing of that, and nothing has to be repeated to him. Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿إنّا نَحْنُ نَـزَّلْنا الذِّكْرَ وإنّا لَهُ لَحافِظُونَ﴾ [al-Ḥijr: 9] ("It is We who sent down the Reminder, and We are surely its guardians").

zajjaj:7-7.t: As for ﴿إلا ما شاءَ اللَّهُ﴾ ("except what Allah wills"), it was said: except what Allah wills, and then He reminds him of it afterwards; and it was said: except what Allah wills to defer of the Qur'an.

zajjaj:11-11.t: ﴿وَيَتَجَنَّبُها الأشْقى﴾: the meaning is ”يَتَجَنَّبُ الذِّكْرى الأشْقى“ ("the most wretched avoids the reminder").

zajjaj:13-13.t: And His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ لا يَمُوتُ فِيها ولا يَحْيا﴾ ("then he will neither die therein nor live"): he does not die a death by which he would find rest from the punishment, nor does he live a life with which he would find the comfort of life.

zajjaj:14-14.t: And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿قَدْ أفْلَحَ مَن تَزَكّى﴾: that is, he has attained lasting permanence and the triumph of bliss. The meaning of ﴿تَزَكّى﴾ is: he increased himself through fear of Allah (taqwā); and the meaning of ”اَلزّاكِي“ is "the growing, the abundant".

zajjaj:16-16.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿بَلْ تُؤْثِرُونَ الحَياةَ الدُّنْيا﴾ ("rather, you prefer the life of this world"). It was also read: ”بَلْ يُؤْثِرُونَ الحَياةَ الدُّنْيا“ ("rather, they prefer…") with yāʾ; but tāʾ is better, because it is related from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb as: ”بَلْ أنْتُمْ تُؤْثِرُونَ الحَياةَ الدُّنْيا“ ("rather, you prefer the life of this world").

zajjaj:18-18.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إنَّ هَذا لَفي الصُّحُفِ الأُولى﴾ ("this is surely in the former scriptures"): He means from His saying ﴿قَدْ أفْلَحَ مَن تَزَكّى﴾ [al-Aʿlā: 14] up to this place; and it was said: rather, the whole sūra.
